The **Men's Ski Cross** event at the **2018 Winter Olympics** in **PyeongChang, South Korea**, was a thrilling and highly competitive race that showcased the speed, skill, and physicality of freestyle skiing. Here’s a detailed breakdown of everything you need to know:

---

### **1. Event Overview**
- **Discipline:** Freestyle Skiing (Ski Cross)
- **Venue:** **Bokwang Phoenix Park** (same venue as snowboarding events)
- **Date:** **February 21, 2018**
- **Format:**
  - **Qualification:** Time trials (seeding runs) to determine rankings for the elimination rounds.
  - **Elimination Rounds:** Heats of 4 skiers each, with the top 2 advancing to the next round until the final.
  - **Final:** A single race determining the medalists (Gold, Silver, Bronze).

---

### **2. Course Details**
- **Length:** ~1,100 meters
- **Vertical Drop:** ~200 meters
- **Features:**
  - Banked turns, rollers, jumps (including a big air section), and tight sections requiring tactical racing.
  - Designed to test speed, technical skill, and physical contact resilience.
- **Conditions:** Cold and firm snow, with some wind affecting visibility in places.

---

### **3. Key Competitors & Favorites**
The field was stacked with experienced racers, including:
- **Bastian Schmid (Austria)** – 2017 World Championship silver medalist.
- **Sergey Ridzik (OAR – Olympic Athletes from Russia)** – 2014 Olympic bronze medalist.
- **Jean Frédéric Chapuis (France)** – 2014 Olympic gold medalist (defending champion).
- **Bady Dallaze (France)** – Strong contender with multiple World Cup podiums.
- **Brice Luccarini (France)** – Experienced racer with World Cup wins.
- **Kevin Drury (Canada)** – Rising star, 2017 X Games gold medalist.
- **David Duncan (Canada)** – Veteran with multiple World Cup podiums.
- **Armin Niederer (Switzerland)** – Consistent performer in World Cups.

*(Note: Defending champion **Jean Frédéric Chapuis** crashed in training before the event and did not compete, removing a major favorite.)*

---

### **4. Race Summary**
#### **Qualification (Seeding Runs)**
- **Fastest Time:** **Sergey Ridzik (OAR)** – 1:09.61
- **Other Top Qualifiers:**
  - **Bastian Schmid (AUT)** – 1:09.62
  - **Kevin Drury (CAN)** – 1:09.65
  - **Armin Niederer (SUI)** – 1:09.76
- **Notable:** The top seeds avoided early-round matchups with each other.

#### **Elimination Rounds**
- **Round of 16:** No major upsets; top skiers advanced.
- **Quarterfinals:**
  - **Heat 1:** Ridzik and Drury advanced.
  - **Heat 2:** Schmid and **Marc Bischofberger (SUI)** advanced.
  - **Heat 3:** Niederer and **Jonathan Midol (FRA)** advanced.
  - **Heat 4:** **David Duncan (CAN)** and **Filip Flisar (SLO)** advanced.
- **Semifinals:**
  - **Semifinal 1:** Ridzik and Drury advanced (Schmid crashed out).
  - **Semifinal 2:** Niederer and Bischofberger advanced (Midol and Duncan eliminated).

#### **Finals**
- **Big Final (Gold Medal Race):**
  - **Sergey Ridzik (OAR)** – **1st Place (Gold)**
  - **Kevin Drury (CAN)** – **2nd Place (Silver)**
  - **Armin Niederer (SUI)** – **3rd Place (Bronze)**
  - **Marc Bischofberger (SUI)** – 4th Place
- **Small Final (5th–8th Place):**
  - **Bastian Schmid (AUT)** – 5th
  - **David Duncan (CAN)** – 6th
  - **Jonathan Midol (FRA)** – 7th
  - **Filip Flisar (SLO)** – 8th

---
### **5. Medalists & Results**
| **Medal** | **Athlete**          | **Country**               | **Time (Final)** |
|-----------|----------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| **Gold**  | Sergey Ridzik        | OAR (Olympic Athletes from Russia) | ~1:10.00* |
| **Silver**| Kevin Drury          | Canada                    | +0.30            |
| **Bronze**| Armin Niederer       | Switzerland               | +0.56            |

*(*Note: Exact final times were close, with Ridzik leading wire-to-wire.)*

---
### **6. Key Moments & Drama**
- **Sergey Ridzik’s Dominance:** Ridzik was the fastest qualifier and won every heat, including the final, with a near-flawless run.
- **Kevin Drury’s Silver:** Drury, a rising star, held off Niederer for silver, marking Canada’s first men’s ski cross Olympic medal.
- **Bastian Schmid’s Crash:** The Austrian favorite crashed in the semifinal, ending his medal hopes.
- **French Struggles:** Without Chapuis (injured), France’s best finisher was Midol in 7th.
- **Tight Racing:** The final was a tactical battle, with Ridzik taking an early lead and holding off challenges from Drury and Niederer.

---
### **7. Controversies & Notable Incidents**
- **Jean Frédéric Chapuis’ Absence:** The 2014 gold medalist crashed in training, suffering a knee injury that ruled him out.
- **Contact in Heats:** Ski cross is known for physical racing, and several heats saw close calls (e.g., Schmid’s crash in the semifinal).
- **OAR (Russia) Participation:** Ridzik competed under the **Olympic Athletes from Russia** flag due to the IOC’s suspension of Russia for doping violations.

---
### **8. Legacy & Impact**
- **Ridzik’s Redemption:** After winning bronze in 2014, Ridzik upgraded to gold in 2018, cementing his status as one of the sport’s best.
- **Canada’s Breakthrough:** Drury’s silver was a historic moment for Canadian men’s ski cross.
- **Course Design:** The Bokwang Phoenix Park course was praised for its technical challenges, though some criticized its lack of big jumps compared to other World Cup venues.

---
### **9. Fun Facts**
- **Oldest Competitor:** **Eril Hemilä (FIN)**, age 35.
- **Youngest Competitor:** **Nikita Novitski (OAR)**, age 20.
- **Most Olympic Medals in Ski Cross (Men):** Sergey Ridzik (Gold in 2018, Bronze in 2014).
- **First Olympic Ski Cross:** The event debuted in **2010 (Vancouver)**.

---
### **10. Where to Watch (Archived Footage)**
- **Olympic Channel (YouTube):** [2018 PyeongChang Men’s Ski Cross Final](https://www.youtube.com)
- **NBC Sports / Olympics.com:** Highlights and replays.

---
### **11. Post-Olympic Careers of Medalists**
- **Sergey Ridzik:** Continued competing, winning **World Cup races** and **2021 World Championship silver**.
- **Kevin Drury:** Became a **consistent World Cup podium finisher**; won **2022 Olympic silver** (Beijing).
- **Armin Niederer:** Retired after the 2018–19 season but remained involved in ski cross as a coach.

---
### **12. Comparison to Other Olympics**
| **Year** | **Gold**               | **Silver**            | **Bronze**            |
|----------|------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| **2010** | Michael Schmid (SUI)   | Andreas Matt (AUT)    | Audun Grønvold (NOR)  |
| **2014** | Jean Frédéric Chapuis  | Arnaud Bovolenta (FRA) | Sergey Ridzik (RUS)   |
| **2018** | Sergey Ridzik (OAR)    | Kevin Drury (CAN)     | Armin Niederer (SUI)  |
| **2022** | Ryan Regez (SUI)       | Kevin Drury (CAN)     | Sergey Ridzik (ROC)   |

*(Note: Ridzik is the only man with **two ski cross Olympic medals**.)*

---
### **Final Thoughts**
The **2018 Men’s Ski Cross** was a **tactical, high-speed battle** with **Sergey Ridzik** emerging as the deserved champion. The race highlighted the **unpredictability** of ski cross, where **one mistake can end a run**, and **physicality** plays as big a role as pure speed. Ridzik’s gold, Drury’s silver, and Niederer’s bronze made for a **memorable Olympic moment** in freestyle skiing history.
